The translator with island 2.1 inside draft

The author, 24 October 2026: “only the box of 2.1 should be retained, it does not make sense to include the 22M deck of abstract, those are the input-output in the translator concept”, and then: “2.1 could be integrated way better in the translator. why a black bezel? why white board spilling on the left and right of 2.1... It should be perfectly integrated.” So the box of 2.1, its three strips, is taken from the signed drawing (commit 7da1b55's fixed.svg) and laid EDGE TO EDGE in variants 2 to 5. The view is exactly the frames' outer edge. Its paper is hidden except inside each frame, and its decks, legend and arrows are hidden too. Only its six ids change; its geometry is as signed, scaled and never re-laid. What shows between and round the strips is the machine. Variant 1 is the screen it had, for comparison. Every call of the translator without these options is byte-identical (PROOF.md). Each at size 300: whole, 1/3, 1/20.

0. validated

The translator as validated: the two bubbles on its screen.

translator(x, y, 300)

1. screen

On a screen (r3-2 as revised on 24 October): the box on 2.1's paper, inside a dark bezel. What the author asked to replace.

translator(x, y, 300, inside="workflow", fit="screen")

2. inlay

Inlaid: no screen. The casing is fitted to the box and wraps it edge to edge; the three strips are set into its face, each over an offset darker copy of itself, and the casing shows between them.

translator(x, y, 300, inside="workflow", fit="inlay")

3. rim

The box's border is the machine's frame: the casing is only as wide as the box and the slots' lips, outlined in 2.1's own ink and weight, so the machine reads as a fourth frame round the three.

translator(x, y, 300, inside="workflow", fit="rim")

4. cutaway

Cut away: the casing keeps a wall round an opening into the machine; through it, its inside, a shade of the casing, and the box mounted in it, its wall in shadow at the top and left.

translator(x, y, 300, inside="workflow", fit="cutaway")

5. glass

A glass case: no casing face; the box stands in a lilac-white glass case on the machine's base with its lights, a white highlight on the glass.

translator(x, y, 300, inside="workflow", fit="glass")
